Fetch a soul's SOUL.md body verbatim and write it where the target framework
reads it:

  hermes    ~/.hermes/SOUL.md (the default)
  claude    ~/.claude/SOUL.md (--link also adds an @-import to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
  cursor    ./.cursor/rules/soul.mdc (wrapped in mdc frontmatter)
  openclaw  <workspace>/SOUL.md (default ~/.openclaw/workspace/SOUL.md; --workspace
            picks the agent when several are configured)

Without --target the harness is detected from marker directories (.hermes,
.claude, .cursor, .openclaw) in the working directory, then your home
directory; hermes is the fallback. --path overrides everything and writes the
body verbatim to that exact file (the cursor wrapper applies only when
--target cursor is set explicitly).

This is the one command that counts as a download on positronick.com. An
existing file is only overwritten after a confirmation prompt (interactive)
or with --force.

Usage:
  positronick soul install <slug> [flags]

Flags:
      --force              overwrite an existing file without asking
  -h, --help               help for install
      --link               claude target only: add an @-import line to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
      --path string        write the SOUL.md to this exact file instead of the target's path
      --target string      install target: hermes, claude, cursor or openclaw (default: detected harness, else hermes)
      --workspace string   openclaw target only: the OpenClaw agent id or workspace dir; default: the single configured agent

Global Flags:
      --base-url string   override the positronick.com API base URL
      --json              emit machine-readable JSON on stdout
      --no-color          disable color output
      --quiet             suppress progress output on stderr
      --yes               assume yes for confirmation prompts
